correction.note: The Z/3 direction used by D(A4) is from linear characters of A4, not from the group center.

criterion_for_untwisted_DG.invertible_simples: Pairs (z, chi) with z in Z(G) and chi in Hom(G,C*) = Hom(G_ab,C*).
criterion_for_untwisted_DG.nonbaseline_split_signal: There is a nonbaseline ordinary split character-twist value exactly when some chosen invertible labels g_h,g_e1,g_e2 have theta(g_h)^-1 theta(g_e1) theta(g_e2) != 1.
criterion_for_untwisted_DG.group_theoretic_nontriviality_test: The pointed quadratic form of D(G) is nontrivial exactly when the natural map Z(G) -> G_ab is nonzero, equivalently when some central element survives abelianization and some linear character evaluates nontrivially on it.

smallest_natural_nonproduct_candidate.group: Dic_3, the order-12 dicyclic / binary-dihedral group, sometimes denoted Q12
smallest_natural_nonproduct_candidate.why_it_is_first_useful_natural_example: Among nonabelian groups below order 12, S3 and D10 have trivial center, while the order-8 groups D8 and Q8 have center contained in the commutator subgroup. The order-12 dihedral group has the needed phase but is S3 x C2. Dic_3 is the natural order-12 nonproduct example: a^3 is central and a^3 is not in <a^2>, so it survives in G_ab.
smallest_natural_nonproduct_candidate.D_G_twist_witness: In the abelianization, a maps to the square of a C4 generator. A linear character sending that generator to i has chi(a^3)=-1, so the invertible simple (a^3,chi) in D(G) has twist -1.

A4.verdict: trivial for this D(G) split character test
A4.reason: There are pure charge invertibles but no central flux; all invertible twists are 1.

S3.verdict: trivial for this D(G) split character test

abelian_G.reason: Z(G)=G and G_ab=G, so the evaluation pairing can be nontrivial. However this is just a pointed finite metric group calculation.

D8_order_8_dihedral.reason: For the square dihedral group, the central 180-degree rotation lies in the commutator subgroup and dies in abelianization, so every linear character is trivial on it.

D12_order_12_dihedral.reason: For the dihedral group with rotation order 6, the central 180-degree rotation does survive in abelianization, so some linear character sees it. However this group is isomorphic to S3 x C2, so it is not the desired nonproduct example.

Dic3_order_12_dicyclic.reason: The central element a^3 survives in the C4 abelianization.

Q8.reason: The central element -1 lies in the commutator subgroup and dies in abelianization, so every linear character is trivial on it.

interpretation_for_search.weak_useful: A D(G) with Z(G)->G_ab nonzero can produce nonbaseline phases on the ordinary split presentation.
interpretation_for_search.strong_useful_for_exotic_detection: This is probably still not useful for the main Yasui strategy, because the separated test only sees the pointed metric group, not the nonabelian double data.
interpretation_for_search.recommended_filter: Do not brute-force D(G) merely because G has nontrivial abelianization. First check whether a central element survives in G_ab; otherwise the split character scan is guaranteed baseline.
